loadError: The settings could not be loaded

account.title: Sign-in security
account.description: How you sign in to {appName}: passkeys, the authenticator app for the emergency password, and your other sessions.

toasts.backupCodesRenewed: New recovery codes created. The previous ones no longer work.
toasts.sessionsRevoked: All other sessions were signed out.

mode.title: Operating mode
mode.description: How browsers reach this installation. The mode decides whether passkeys are available.
mode.localDescription: Reachable via IP address or localhost, without a public domain. Admins sign in with the emergency password and an authenticator code.
mode.publicDescription: Reachable via your own domain over HTTPS. Passkeys are available.

publicUrl.label: Public URL
publicUrl.hint: Exactly the address browsers open, without a path. It defines the passkey domain and the Entra redirect URI.

environment.title: The server still runs with a different address
environment.description: RESTOW_PUBLIC_URL is set to {url}. Sign-in and passkeys follow that value until you change it in the .env file and restart {appName}.

localConfirm.title: Switch to local mode?
localConfirm.description: Without a public URL, passkeys stop working. Admins then sign in with the emergency password and an authenticator code only.

readiness.title: Passkey readiness
readiness.description: Passkeys bind to a domain served over HTTPS. {appName} checks the configuration, and the server tries to reach its own public address with full certificate validation.
readiness.ready: Passkeys are offered on this installation.
readiness.notReady: Passkeys are not offered. Admins sign in with the emergency password and an authenticator code.

reasons.mode_not_public: Local mode binds no domain, which passkeys require.
reasons.no_public_url: No valid public URL is set.
reasons.not_https: The public URL is not served over HTTPS.
reasons.origin_mismatch: Your browser is on a different address than the public URL.

readiness.checkFailed: The check could not be run

status.ok: The public address answers over HTTPS with a trusted certificate.
status.skipped: Runs only in public mode with an HTTPS public URL, not for localhost.
status.unreachable: The server could not reach its own public address. A firewall or missing hairpin routing can cause this even when browsers reach it without problems.
status.timeout: The public address did not answer within 8 seconds.
status.certificate_invalid: The certificate is not trusted, for example because it is self-signed or expired. Browsers refuse passkeys on such connections.
status.unexpected_response: Something other than {appName} answers at this address. Check the reverse proxy and the DNS records.

mail.title: Notification mail
mail.description: {appName} sends reports, alerts and invitations through this transport. The journal intake for the archive is separate and only receives.

notConfigured.title: No mail transport is set up
notConfigured.description: Mail is optional. Without a transport {appName} sends no alert or report e-mails, and invitations and set-password links are not sent by mail: you copy the link and pass it on yourself.

remove.title: Remove mail configuration
remove.description: Deletes the notification transport and destroys the stored SMTP password. {appName} sends no reports, alerts or invitations until a new transport is set up.
remove.confirmDescription: Notifications stop right away. The stored SMTP password is deleted and cannot be recovered.

smtp.securityNoneWarning: Without encryption, the password and every message travel in plain text. Use this only for a relay inside your own network.
smtp.usernameHint: Leave empty if the server does not require authentication.
smtp.passwordHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
smtp.passwordKeep: A password is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
smtp.passwordAgain: Server or username changed. Enter the password for them.

graph.hint: Sends as the {appName} app registration through Microsoft Graph. Requires the Mail.Send application permission with admin consent; an application access policy can restrict it to the sender mailbox.

appMissing.title: App registration not configured
appMissing.description: No Microsoft 365 app registration is set up. Graph sends as that app; set it up under Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app, and grant it Mail.Send.

graph.passwordRemoved: Saving with Microsoft Graph deletes the stored SMTP password.
graph.tenantIdHint: Tenant ID or a verified domain of the tenant the sender mailbox belongs to.
graph.tenantIdDefault: Leave empty to use {tenant} from the server configuration.

test.title: Test message
test.description: Sends a test notification with the values shown above, including unsaved changes.
test.success: Handed over for {recipient} in {duration}. Check the inbox, including the spam folder.
test.failed: The test message could not be sent

reasons.timeout: No answer within 20 seconds. Check host, port and firewall.
reasons.graph_app_missing: No Microsoft 365 app registration is set up (Installation → Microsoft multi-tenant app).
reasons.graph_tenant_missing: No Entra tenant is set for the sender mailbox.
reasons.transport_error: The mail system refused the connection or the message.

microsoftApp.title: Microsoft 365 app registration
microsoftApp.description: The multi-tenant backup app in your own Microsoft Entra directory. Customers grant it admin consent; {appName} then backs up and restores their mailboxes and OneDrives with it.
microsoftApp.loadError: The app registration could not be loaded.

status.title: Status

source.none: Not set up yet. Follow the four steps below.

status.environmentNote: The values come from the server environment (ENTRA_CLIENT_ID with ENTRA_CLIENT_SECRET or ENTRA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH). They take precedence and can only be changed there. To manage the registration here instead, remove those variables and restart {appName}.
status.environmentPartial: Some ENTRA_CLIENT_* values are set in the server environment, but not enough to use them. They are ignored; the registration entered here is used.

problems.certificate_unreadable: The certificate file named in ENTRA_CLIENT_CERT_PATH cannot be read on this server.
problems.certificate_invalid: The certificate lacks its private key or the certificate itself. Upload it again.
problems.document_unreadable: The saved registration cannot be opened with the current master key (RESTOW_MASTER_KEY). Enter it again.
problems.authority_host_invalid: The saved login host is no longer accepted. Enter the registration again and choose one of Microsoft's login hosts.

expiry.soon: {days, plural, one {Expires in # day} other {Expires in # days}}
expiry.warning: Create the next credential now: add it in Entra, enter it here, then delete the old one. Never the other way round.

register.title: Register the app
register.description: Once, in your own Microsoft Entra directory. The same app serves every customer.
register.path: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open:
register.name: Name: for example {appName}. Customers see it when they grant consent.
register.accountTypesValue: Accounts in any organizational directory (Any Microsoft Entra ID tenant - Multitenant)
register.redirect: Redirect URI: select the platform Web and enter exactly this value:
register.redirectMissing: No public URL is set yet. Set it under Installation → Server; the redirect URI is derived from it.
register.register: Select Register. The overview page then shows the two values you enter in step 4:
register.openAdminCenter: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center

permissions.title: API permissions
permissions.description: Under API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions, add exactly these permissions:
permissions.delegated: Then add openid and profile under Delegated permissions. They grant no data access; they only let a customer's admin confirm who they are after the consent.
permissions.consent: Finally select this button on the API permissions page:
permissions.consentHint: This consents in your own directory. Customers consent through the link {appName} creates for each Microsoft 365 source.
permissions.pitfall: The most common mistake: with Mail.Read the backup runs, but every restore fails with 403. The same applies to Calendars.ReadWrite and Contacts.ReadWrite.
permissions.sites: Sites.ReadWrite.All is deliberately not requested: SharePoint is not part of this version, and it would widen the consent needlessly.
permissions.mailSend: Mail.Send only when notifications are sent through Microsoft Graph instead of SMTP.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.description: {appName} signs in as the app with a certificate (recommended) or a client secret. Set up one of them.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.create: Create a key pair, for example with OpenSSL:
certificate.upload: Under Certificates & secrets → Certificates → Upload certificate, upload restow-entra.crt (the public part only).
certificate.enter: In step 4, upload restow-entra.pem (private key and certificate). The private key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
certificate.benefit: No secret in plain text, and renewable without downtime.

secret.title: Client secret
secret.create: Under Certificates & secrets → Client secrets, select New client secret. Choose at most 24 months; Microsoft allows no longer term.
secret.valueTitle: Copy the Value, not the Secret ID
secret.value: Right after creating the secret, copy the Value column. Entra shows it only once; the Secret ID next to it is not the secret.
secret.rotate: {appName} warns 60 days before the secret expires. To rotate, create a new secret, enter it here, and only then delete the old one in Entra.

enter.title: Enter in {appName}
enter.description: Stored encrypted with the master key of this installation. The secret and the private key are never shown again.
enter.readOnly: The server environment provides the registration; there is nothing to enter here.

form.tenantIdHint: Your own directory, used for the connection test. A GUID or a verified domain.
form.secretStored: Stored. Leave empty to keep it
form.secretHint: The Value column from Certificates & secrets, not the Secret ID.
form.secretKeep: A secret is stored. Leave the field empty to keep it.
form.secretAgain: The Application ID or login host changed. Enter the secret for it.
form.expiresAtHint: As shown in Entra. {appName} warns 60 days before.
form.certificateHint: An unencrypted RSA key and the matching certificate, one after the other.
form.certificateKeep: A certificate is stored ({thumbprint}). Upload or paste a new one to replace it.
form.certificateAgain: The Application ID or login host changed. Upload the certificate for it.
form.uploadFailed: The file could not be read.
form.authorityHostHint: Only for national clouds. Leave empty for the global Microsoft cloud.

validation.guid: Enter the Application (client) ID: 32 hexadecimal digits with hyphens.
validation.tenantId: Enter a directory ID (GUID) or a verified domain such as contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
validation.secretIsId: This is the Secret ID. Copy the Value column instead; Entra shows it only right after creating the secret.
validation.credentialRequired: Enter a client secret or upload a certificate.
validation.credentialConflict: Enter either a client secret or a certificate, not both.
validation.privateKeyMissing: The private key (BEGIN PRIVATE KEY) is missing.
validation.privateKeyEncrypted: The private key is protected by a password. Export it without one (OpenSSL option -nodes).
validation.privateKeyInvalid: The private key cannot be read.
validation.keyMismatch: The private key does not belong to this certificate.
validation.certificateNotYetValid: The certificate is not valid yet.
validation.authorityHost: Enter one of Microsoft's login hosts, for example https://login.microsoftonline.us.

test.title: Test connection
test.description: Requests a Microsoft Graph token as the app in your directory and compares the granted application permissions with what {appName} needs.
test.needsSave: Save the registration first; the test uses the saved values.
test.unsaved: The test uses the saved registration, not the unsaved changes above.
test.success: The connection works and every required permission is granted.

reasons.invalid_secret: Entra rejected the client secret. Usually the Secret ID was entered instead of the Value. Create a new secret and copy its Value.
reasons.secret_expired: The client secret has expired. Create a new one under Certificates & secrets and enter it here.
reasons.app_not_found: This directory has no app with this Application (client) ID. Check both IDs from the app's overview page.
reasons.tenant_not_found: This directory does not exist. Check the Directory (tenant) ID.
reasons.credential_missing: Entra expected a client secret or certificate and accepted none. Enter the credential again.
reasons.invalid_certificate: Entra does not accept the certificate. Upload the matching .crt under Certificates & secrets → Certificates.
reasons.consent_missing: No application permission is granted yet. Select Grant admin consent on the API permissions page.
reasons.permissions_missing: Required permissions are missing. Add them under API permissions and grant admin consent again.
reasons.network: Microsoft Entra could not be reached from this server. Check the outbound connection (DNS, firewall, proxy).
reasons.other: Entra refused the sign-in. The error code below helps with the diagnosis.

test.missing: {count, plural, one {# required permission is missing.} other {# required permissions are missing.}}
test.readOnly: {granted} was granted instead of {expected}: backups would run, restores would fail with 403.

remove.title: Remove the app registration
remove.description: {appName} can no longer reach Microsoft 365: backups, restores and directory syncs of every tenant stop until a registration is entered again.
remove.confirmDescription: The client secret or certificate is deleted and cannot be recovered. Backups and restores of every Microsoft 365 source stop.

inline.title: Set up the Microsoft 365 app registration first
inline.description: Tenants can be connected once the backup app is registered in Microsoft Entra and entered here. Changes apply right away, without a restart.

passkeys.title: Your passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in without a password using Touch ID, Windows Hello, your phone or a security key. Passkeys are bound to {domain}.
passkeys.descriptionNoDomain: Sign in without a password using Touch ID, Windows Hello, your phone or a security key.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser cannot create passkeys. Use a current browser to add one.
passkeys.empty: You have no passkey yet. Until you add one, you sign in with the emergency password and an authenticator code.
passkeys.emptyNoAuthenticator: You have no passkey and no authenticator app yet. Add a passkey here or set up the authenticator app below.
passkeys.emptySso: You have no passkey yet. Until you add one, you sign in with your Microsoft account.
passkeys.emptyNotReady: You have no passkey. Passkeys can be added once passkey readiness is reached.
passkeys.notReadyMember: Passkeys are not available on this installation yet. Your administrator enables them by running {appName} on its own HTTPS domain.
passkeys.loadError: Your passkeys could not be loaded

addDialog.title: Add a passkey
addDialog.description: Give the passkey a name you will recognise later, then confirm on your device.
addDialog.name: Name
addDialog.nameHint: Only for you, to tell your passkeys apart.

removeDialog.title: Remove passkey?
removeDialog.description: “{name}” can no longer be used to sign in. Without a passkey you sign in with the emergency password and an authenticator code.
removeDialog.descriptionSso: “{name}” can no longer be used to sign in. Without a passkey you sign in with your Microsoft account.

errors.cancelled: The passkey dialog was cancelled or timed out. Nothing was changed.
errors.alreadyRegistered: This authenticator already holds a passkey for your account.
errors.domain: This browser address does not match the passkey domain. Open {appName} via its public URL and try again.
errors.userVerification: The authenticator cannot verify you with a PIN or biometrics, which {appName} requires.
errors.verificationFailed: The server could not verify the new passkey. Please try again.
errors.generic: The passkey action failed. Please try again.

authenticator.title: Authenticator app
authenticator.description: Your emergency password works only together with a six-digit code from an app on your phone. {appName} asks for it right after the password.
authenticator.enabledDescription: {appName} asks for a code from your authenticator app every time you sign in with your password. If your phone is lost, sign in with a recovery code instead, then move the authenticator to your new phone.
authenticator.requiredDescription: Your emergency password cannot be used without an authenticator app: {appName} accepts it only together with a code from the app. Set it up so you can still sign in when your passkey is not at hand.
authenticator.loadError: Your sign-in methods could not be loaded

setup.title: Set up your authenticator app
setup.replaceTitle: Move the authenticator to a new phone
setup.description: Any app for time-based codes (TOTP) works.
setup.passwordLead: Confirm with your password. {appName} then creates the key for your authenticator app.
setup.replaceWarning: Your current authenticator stops working as soon as you continue. Keep the new phone at hand and finish the setup right away.

steps.open: Open an authenticator app on your phone, for example Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password or Bitwarden, and add an account.
steps.scan: Scan this QR code with the app.
steps.enter: Enter the six-digit code the app now shows.

setup.qrLabel: QR code with the key for your authenticator app
setup.manualHint: Add the account by hand with this key: time-based, six digits, every 30 seconds.
setup.keyCopyFailed: The key could not be copied. Select and copy it by hand.
setup.codeHint: If the code is refused, check that your phone sets its time automatically.

codes.enabled: The authenticator app is set up. From now on {appName} asks for a code after your password.
codes.title: Recovery codes
codes.lead: Each code works once, in place of a code from the app, for example when your phone is lost. Keep them in your password manager or print them: {appName} shows them only now.
codes.copyFailed: The codes could not be copied. Select and copy them by hand.
codes.fileNote: Each code works once. Keep this file somewhere safe and offline.
codes.acknowledge: I have stored the recovery codes somewhere safe.

regenerate.title: New recovery codes
regenerate.description: Creates ten new recovery codes. The previous codes stop working immediately.
regenerate.passwordLead: Confirm with your password to create the new codes.

errors.code: The code is not correct or has expired. Check the time on your phone and enter the current code.
errors.tooManyAttempts: Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.
errors.alreadyEnabled: An authenticator app is already set up for this account.
errors.notEnabled: The setup was not started or has expired. Please start again.
errors.generic: The authenticator setup failed. Please try again.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.description: Sign out every other browser and device where your account is signed in. This browser stays signed in.
sessions.confirmDescription: Every other browser and device signed in with your account is signed out immediately.

validation.originOnly: Enter the address only, without a path, for example https://restow.example.com.
validation.domainRequired: Use a domain name. Passkeys cannot be bound to an IP address.
validation.passwordRequired: Enter the password for this server and username.
validation.tenantId: Enter a tenant ID or a verified domain such as contoso.onmicrosoft.com.
validation.host: Enter a host name or an IP address.

errors.setupIncomplete: The setup is not complete yet. Finish the setup wizard first.
errors.mailNotConfigured: No mail transport is configured yet.
errors.masterKey: The server has no valid master key (RESTOW_MASTER_KEY), so it cannot store the password encrypted.
errors.microsoftAppManaged: The app registration is set in the server environment and can only be changed there.
errors.microsoftAppNotConfigured: Save the app registration before testing it.
